title: Judging a Forecast: Is it Worth Patrolling? (PAI, PEI & The 4 Traps)
simple_summary: A computer model can look very flashy and still be totally useless. Two simple scores tell commanders if a model is genuinely helping or just guessing: PAI (is it better than chance?) and PEI (how close is it to perfection?).
key_concept: PAI > 1 means the flagged zone captured more crime than random patrol. PEI near 1.0 means optimal efficiency. Also avoid the Feedback Loop trap by always keeping a baseline patrol floor everywhere.
recommended_action: Check PAI/PEI monthly. If a model drops below 1.5, re-calibrate. Always maintain at least a 20-30% baseline patrol floor in unpredicted beats.

dataset_sample.verdict: Trap Detected: Patrols only found what they were told to look for

non_tech_takeaway: Predict places and times, never people. A good model informs human judgment; it never replaces the officer on the beat.
